transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in today because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. 

My kitchen table is completely covered right now with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. I sit down there to try and tackle it, and I just... I don't know which thing to do first. I end up just sitting there looking at it until the whole day is gone.
Has something specific happened recently that started these problems?

Well, it's really been causing this much trouble for... I'd say about a year and three months now. That was when my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and all his daily arrangements. I just haven't been able to keep up with it all since then.
Do you feel that these problems started after your husband began needing more help?

Well, they definitely got a lot worse when he needed more help, but... honestly, no, they didn't just start then. I've always struggled with this sort of thing, even way back when I was a little girl. 

I remember my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but... careless. I was always forgetting my books or my homework. They constantly had to remind me to just finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside. So, I guess it's always been there, it's just... it's just so much harder to manage now with everything else on my plate.
When you were a child, did you have trouble paying attention?

Yes, I did. Like I said, I was always forgetting things, and my teachers were always getting after me for not paying attention. I'd be looking out the window, or just daydreaming, and I wouldn't hear a word they said. It was hard for me to focus on anything for very long, especially if it was something I wasn't interested in.
Have you noticed that your thinking or memory has gotten worse compared with how you were before?

No, I wouldn't say my memory or thinking has gotten worse, really. It's just... the same as it's always been, just more of a problem now because I have so much more I have to keep track of with my husband. I don't feel like I'm losing my mind or anything like that, I just can't seem to stay on top of all the details.
Before age 12, were you already having these attention and organization problems?

Yes, definitely. Like I mentioned before, even when I was a little girl, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always forgetting my books and my homework. They constantly had to remind me to just finish my seatwork before they'd let me go outside for recess. So, yes, the organization and attention issues have been there since long before I was 12.
